headline: Strong India, recovering TSN; UK struggles

highlights: TSI volumes grew 8% YoY to 5.98mt on drawdown of inventory in seasonally weak monsoon quarter, while benefit of Auto contracts negated longs weakness driving EBITDA to INR100bn (up 23% YoY).

Europe remained mixed: TSN saw EBITDA improve to EUR72mn from EUR4mn in Q1FY27 as the DSP restarted, while TSUK continued to report losses of GBP147/t on low volumes absorbing entire costs amid weak market impacted by imports.
Going forward, India is expected to lead the H2 recovery, supported by higher volumes and improved steel realizations.
Mgmt. reiterated its preference for value-led growth, with near-term capex focused on downstream capacities and a richer product mix, while major upstream additions planned remain on track.
valuation: In Europe, TSUK is targeting near breakeven by Q4FY27 as excess inventory gradually normalizes, while sustaining the DSP ramp-up remains key to TSN's recovery.
Other important points: • FY27 cost efficiency program target: INR71.4bn of which INR18bn achieved in H1. • Capex: Q2 INR32.80bn; H1FY27 INR68bn.
DRI-EAF remains the reference case, while multiple alternatives are being evaluated.
watch: In Europe, TSUK is targeting near breakeven by Q4FY27 as excess inventory gradually normalizes, while sustaining the DSP ramp-up remains key to TSN's recovery.

Key monitorables include: (a) sustainability of the domestic steel spreads, (b) timely execution of capex at NINL/ Meramandali debottlenecking, (c) rising debt levels, (d) resolution of TSN's regulatory and decarbonization-related uncertainties, and (e) progress on the Port Talbot EAF project for early breakeven.
